requirement:
`habeas mdbook` automatically generates one documented-coverage-gaps
subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`,
whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.
rationale:
`requirements.test-coverage.index` has three obligations. First, `habeas mdbook` generates a documented-coverage-gaps subchapter. Second, it generates exactly one, under the requirements index. Third, it does so whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.

- **Explicitly placed index:** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` uses a `{requirements-index}` directive in an appendix chapter.
  - It filters the index's sub-items for chapters named "Documented coverage gaps" and asserts exactly one.
  - It asserts the chapter's path is `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md` and its `parent_names` is `["Requirements index"]`.
  - It asserts the index content links to it.
  - It asserts the index has 6 sub-items: five requirement pages plus the coverage page.
- **Automatically generated index:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no directive, so the index is generated by default.
  - It asserts exactly one coverage chapter under the generated top-level "Requirements index", with path `requirements-index/coverage.md` and the correct parent.
  - It asserts the index links to the chapter.
  - It asserts the detail pages are separate from the coverage chapter.
- **Hierarchy:** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` covers a nested, differently named and placed index, both numbered and unnumbered.
  - It asserts the coverage chapter sits under that index, with the inherited `parent_names` and section number.
  - It asserts the parent's sub-items count is 2, so no duplicate coverage chapter is generated.
  - It asserts the parent links to the chapter and that the generated chapter has content.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. Together they cover both index modes, the count of one, the parent placement, and the link from the index. I found no plausible violation of the text that these assertions would accept.

text: subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`,
whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
